value.text: In an April 16, 2026 official statement as NSA director, Joshua Rudd said AI research and development is constant and helps stay ahead of foreign adversaries also developing AI tools. In February 2026 statements, Rudd agreed that China is aggressively seeking advanced AI chips to accelerate AI-enhanced weapons and said advanced AI chips are foundational to AI superiority and national security. value.text: In July 2025, the White House released “Winning the AI Race: America’s AI Action Plan,” which it described as identifying over 90 federal policy actions across innovation, infrastructure, and international diplomacy and security. In March 2026, the White House issued a national AI legislative framework and said it looked forward to working with Congress to turn the framework into legislation. A September 2026 executive order directed executive-branch departments and agencies to use “Super Intelligence” and “SI” instead of “Artificial Intelligence” and “AI” in official communications. A June 2026 executive order promoted advanced AI innovation and security, including a voluntary framework with AI developers, while stating that one section did not authorize mandatory government licensing, preclearance, or permitting for new AI models.

value.text: The NSA said U.S.-China frontier AI competition has major national security implications and, with the FBI and CISA, warned that China-based AI companies are illicitly distilling U.S. frontier AI capabilities. The agency released cybersecurity guidance intended to help national security system owners and Defense Industrial Base companies deploy and operate AI systems securely, and it stressed protecting AI supply-chain data. value.text: OMB's March 2024 memorandum directed agencies to advance AI governance and innovation while managing risks, including minimum risk management practices for AI uses affecting public rights and safety. value.text: In May 2026, Deputy NIST Director Craig Burkhardt invited technically capable organizations to join the NIST AI Consortium and said NIST was seeking to expand AI measurement efforts by harnessing the broader community’s interests and capabilities. value.text: NIST Information Technology Laboratory states that it led development of a framework to better manage risks to individuals, organizations, and society associated with AI. ITL describes the NIST AI RMF as voluntary guidelines that can be used as a basis for standards, and says it develops technical resources and guidelines and leads NIST participation in voluntary consensus standards for super intelligence. value.text: In supplied remarks, Hegseth described responsible AI at the War Department as objectively truthful, securely employed, and lawful, while rejecting DEI and social justice constraints and saying the department will not use models that won't allow it to fight wars. He framed military AI as a race in which moving too slowly risks national security, and he called for acceleration, experimentation, and an AI-first warfighting force. He announced GenAI.mil as a secure generative AI platform and later announced Google Gemini and xAI's Grok as frontier AI model partners for the department. He also said U.S. policy is to sustain and enhance global AI dominance and that the department must ensure U.S. military AI dominance so adversaries cannot exploit the technology against national security interests or citizens.

value.text: Michael Ellis said AI could reduce tasks that once took months or years to hours or days and called it a potential “game changer” that could fundamentally reshape the intelligence business. He said such models can bring knowledge and capabilities previously held only by nation-states to a wide range of actors, and that AI would help CIA analysts draft key judgments, edit for clarity, and compare drafts against tradecraft standards. Ellis said CIA is entering commercial partnerships in areas including AI and that it should not let private companies dictate how and when CIA makes lawful use of their technologies. He described competition with China as unlike anything the United States has faced and said the U.S. must continue to lead the AI race, citing President Trump’s AI Action Plan as setting up the private sector to win that race.

value.text: CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig said in October 2026 that superintelligence holds the promise to transform the global economy and financial markets. value.text: Veronica E. Hinton-authored OPM materials state that OPM is implementing requirements of the AI in Government Act of 2020 and issued AI classification and talent acquisition guidance intended to help agencies hire and retain a highly skilled AI workforce. A December 2025 memo states that OPM granted governmentwide direct-hire authority for certain information technology, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, and other technical positions and says attracting and retaining such talent is essential to safeguarding Federal systems and modernizing operations. The materials also describe an OPM AI job analysis survey to validate AI competencies and guidance supporting governmentwide skills-based hiring for AI, data, and technology talent in compliance with Executive Order 14110. The AI classification guidance discusses using “Artificial Intelligence or AI” as a parenthetical title for occupational series performing AI work the majority of the time and describes AI as enhancing Federal employees’ capabilities and augmenting work.
